set.body:
Journey: Bring in. Track: engine and console.

Outcome
An operator imports a converted study from a folder on the server, session by session if needed. The curator reviews the result in the browser and accepts it.

Acceptance
1. The operator import command gains two options: add against the current release of a dataset that already has releases, and stop at a candidate instead of accepting. The engine supports both already: DurableImports.resume takes a publish flag and ImportPlan carries a base. Today the command passes publish and the default plan.
2. The command prints a console link to the candidate. The console has a candidate review page at that link with the same preview as an upload: coverage by data type, findings, and Accept. A second import while a candidate is pending has a clear outcome.
3. A study larger than the browser upload limits (8 GiB in total, 2 GiB per file) imports this way. Record wall time and peak memory for a study of at least 5 GiB.
4. An interrupted import resumes with the same idempotency key and does not create a second release.

Not in scope
A browser screen that starts server-side imports. Lifting the 10,000-entry limit: that is parked as W02.1 and comes forward only if the chosen study needs it.

Start from
- modules/service/src/main/scala/sanctity/app/RepositoryCli.scala line 46: today's import begins a durable import and publishes immediately.
- modules/application/src/main/scala/sanctity/application/DurableImports.scala lines 24 to 62, and BrowserUploads.scala for additions against a base release.
- modules/http/src/main/resources/sanctity/ui/upload.js: the preview to reuse.

Evidence
A PostgreSQL integration test for adding against a base release from the command line. One browser step in the IN6 rehearsal.
set.title: IN4: Import a staged BIDS folder on the server and review it in the browser
